currentContext.expansion: During FY 2025-26, the Company continued to invest in capacity enhancement, process automation and infrastructure development across its Cattle Feed and Dairy Divisions. In the Cattle Feed segment, an Automatic Batching System was commissioned and capitalised at the Swaminathapuram Cattle Feed Plant (Tamil Nadu) at a cost of Rs.548.48 lakhs to improve process automation and production accuracy; a new Hammer Mill was commissioned at the Vedagiri Cattle Feed Plant (Kerala) for Rs.95.78 lakhs to improve grinding efficiency and production capacity; and a Molasses Storage Tank was capitalised at the Irinjalakuda Cattle Feed Unit (Kerala) for Rs.47.13 lakhs to strengthen raw-material storage and handling. In the Dairy Division, an Ice Cream Cup and Cone Filling Machine was commissioned at the Konikkara Unit (Kerala) for Rs.27.23 lakhs to support product diversification and manufacturing efficiency, and a Cold Room Container was capitalised at the Thalayuth Unit (Tamil Nadu) for Rs.16.21 lakhs to augment storage and cold-chain management. The Company is also constructing a 30,000 sq. ft. warehouse at its Irinjalakuda Cattle Feed Facility (Kerala); as of 31 March 2026, Rs.240.55 lakhs had been incurred, with completion and capitalisation expected during the next financial year (FY27). Separately, in the prior year the Company had incurred capital expenditure of Rs.1,039.00 lakhs on the Tuticorin Warehouse Project (Oil Cake Processing Division) to strengthen logistics, raw-material handling and inventory-management infrastructure, and had commissioned Blast Freezers at its Vedagiri and Konikkara ice-cream facilities.

risks.note: High and unpredictable prices for essential feed ingredients (soybean meal, rice bran, maize, copra cake) driven by supply-chain disruptions, irregular weather, government interventions, geopolitical factors and competing demand from food/biofuel industries continue to pressure margins; near-term visibility on corrections remains limited.

Government and Cooperative feed players in Kerala create an uneven competitive landscape; government control over milk prices limits dairy farmers' capacity to absorb feed cost increases, impacting demand for the Company's products in this segment and constraining pricing flexibility.

risks.risk: Exchange-rate fluctuations on imported copra cake
risks.note: A significant portion of copra cake is imported from Sri Lanka and the Philippines; volatility in INR/USD and INR/PHP exchange rates poses material risk to procurement costs, with a weaker rupee eroding margins, especially during periods of domestic price pressure.

risks.risk: Copra cake availability / coconut oil price volatility
risks.note: While rising coconut oil prices support the Oil Cake Processing Division's profitability, scarcity of de-oiled copra cake - driven by rising Asia-Pacific demand and, going into FY27, a lower coconut crop yield - poses a challenge to feed production and raises the risk of supply constraints and pricing pressure.

Labour-intensive operations in Kerala face ongoing shortages, resulting in rising wage costs and operational strain, especially in margin-sensitive segments; mitigated through mechanisation, productivity initiatives and long-term wage settlements.

Growth in the Ice Cream and Dairy Divisions has increased dealer and distributor credit exposure; delays in receivables or distributor defaults may create liquidity pressures despite controlled credit policies and periodic reviews.

Monsoon failures, erratic rainfall, and shifts in cropping patterns towards higher-value cash crops reduce the availability of essential oilseeds and grains, tightening raw-material supply for the feed business.

risks.risk: Structural decline of the core Kerala market
risks.note: Shrinking cattle population and declining commercial dairy farming in Kerala - the Company's key home market - alongside government-controlled milk procurement prices, structurally constrain feed and milk demand, requiring the Company to lean on Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and new geographies for growth.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: KSE Limited is a nearly six-decade-old, Kerala-headquartered diversified agri-business and a trusted market leader in cattle feed and coconut oil cake processing across Southern India, with interests spanning animal nutrition, edible oils and dairy products.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: KSE Limited, incorporated in 1963 and headquartered in Irinjalakuda, Kerala, manufactures and markets cattle and poultry feed under its Animal Feed Division, undertakes solvent extraction and oil cake processing including coconut oil refining under its Oil Cake Processing Division, and produces milk and milk products including ice cream under its Dairy Division. Its flagship brands - KS Cattle Feed, KS Poultry Feed, and Vesta Ice Cream and Dairy Products (Ghee, Paneer & Curd) - enjoy strong brand equity across Kerala and neighbouring states, serving farmers and consumers through an extensive distribution and dealer network.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Rising per capita meat and dairy consumption, driven by increasing disposable incomes, urbanisation and changing dietary preferences, is structurally boosting demand for formulated feeds
- Rapid commercialisation of livestock and dairy farming, with a steady rise in high-yielding exotic and crossbred cattle populations dependent on nutritionally balanced compound feeds, underpins structural growth in the animal feed industry
- Government livestock-development schemes, subsidies and incentives for feed mills are encouraging industry growth and farmer adoption of compound feeds
- Growing emphasis on feed quality/safety and scientifically formulated, contamination-free feed is driving demand for premium and specialised products
- Poultry feed demand continues to grow rapidly on favourable production and consumption trends, offering the Company incremental revenue and margin opportunities
- Shrinking cattle population and declining dairy-farming activity in Kerala, driven partly by stagnant milk procurement prices, is a structural headwind reducing feed demand in the Company's key home market
- Subsidised competition from Government and Cooperative feed producers in Kerala limits pricing flexibility in price-sensitive markets
- Raw-material price volatility (maize, soybean meal, de-oiled rice bran, copra cake and other key ingredients) continues to affect production costs and margin predictability
- Significant copra cake imports from the Philippines, Indonesia and Sri Lanka expose the Company to INR/USD exchange-rate volatility, with a weaker rupee eroding margins
- Improved demand and better realisations in coconut oil and refined coconut oil markets, along with effective procurement/advance-contracting strategies, are supporting the Oil Cake Processing Division's operating performance
- Enhanced logistics infrastructure (including the Tuticorin warehouse) and integrated supply-chain strengths are expected to support the Oil Cake Processing Division's continued performance, though rising imported raw-material costs and rupee depreciation pose headwinds
- Expanding organised dairy markets and favourable demographic trends are cited as long-term growth opportunities for India's livestock, dairy and food-processing sectors

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Expanding into new geographies beyond established Southern Indian markets, with Maharashtra identified as the first step toward a pan-India presence
- Advancing the specialised animal-nutrition portfolio through products such as Type-1 Feed for high-yielding cattle, Calf Starter Pellets and other life-stage-specific feed solutions
- Strengthening market reach by deepening the dealer and distribution network across operating regions
- Driving product diversification to address evolving livestock nutritional needs across a wider range of customer segments
- Creating lasting farmer value through scientific advisory services, customised nutrition programmes, veterinary support and continuous farmer engagement
- Continuing investment in infrastructure and manufacturing modernisation - plant modernisation, warehouse infrastructure and process automation - to build a stronger, more efficient manufacturing ecosystem for sustainable growth
- Pursuing innovation and digital transformation across manufacturing and business processes to improve productivity and operational visibility
- Maintaining balance-sheet strength, prudent treasury management and financial discipline to preserve flexibility for future growth opportunities
- Evaluating diversification into complementary sectors, including bio-waste management, as a long-term (presently evaluation-stage) growth avenue
- Strengthening the poultry feed business as a growth driver alongside the traditional cattle-feed business
- Addressing traditional-market demand challenges (Kerala) through strategic planning, dynamic pricing, operational excellence, advance procurement contracts, geographic diversification and continuous product innovation
- The Company distributes profits to shareholders through interim and final dividends declared each year, with the final dividend subject to shareholder approval at the AGM; for FY 2025-26 the Board declared an interim dividend and, per the Notice of AGM, resolved to declare a total dividend of Rs.12.50 per equity share (including the Rs.5 interim dividend already paid), including a final dividend of Rs.7.50 per equity share recommended by the Board, to be paid out of the year's profits.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY 2025-26, the Company continued to invest in capacity enhancement, process automation and infrastructure development across its Cattle Feed and Dairy Divisions. In the Cattle Feed segment, an Automatic Batching System was commissioned and capitalised at the Swaminathapuram Cattle Feed Plant (Tamil Nadu) at a cost of Rs.548.48 lakhs to improve process automation and production accuracy; a new Hammer Mill was commissioned at the Vedagiri Cattle Feed Plant (Kerala) for Rs.95.78 lakhs to improve grinding efficiency and production capacity; and a Molasses Storage Tank was capitalised at the Irinjalakuda Cattle Feed Unit (Kerala) for Rs.47.13 lakhs to strengthen raw-material storage and handling. In the Dairy Division, an Ice Cream Cup and Cone Filling Machine was commissioned at the Konikkara Unit (Kerala) for Rs.27.23 lakhs to support product diversification and manufacturing efficiency, and a Cold Room Container was capitalised at the Thalayuth Unit (Tamil Nadu) for Rs.16.21 lakhs to augment storage and cold-chain management. The Company is also constructing a 30,000 sq. ft. warehouse at its Irinjalakuda Cattle Feed Facility (Kerala); as of 31 March 2026, Rs.240.55 lakhs had been incurred, with completion and capitalisation expected during the next financial year (FY27). Separately, in the prior year the Company had incurred capital expenditure of Rs.1,039.00 lakhs on the Tuticorin Warehouse Project (Oil Cake Processing Division) to strengthen logistics, raw-material handling and inventory-management infrastructure, and had commissioned Blast Freezers at its Vedagiri and Konikkara ice-cream facilities.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Trusted market leader in cattle feed and coconut oil cake processing, built on nearly six decades of operational excellence, industry knowledge and farmer relationships
- SEA Award as highest processor of coconut oil cake, received consecutively for over 35 years
- Extensive distribution network and dealer partnerships across Kerala and expanding presence in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and other neighbouring states
- Strong brand equity in KS Cattle Feed, KS Poultry Feed, and the Vesta Ice Cream and Dairy Products range
- Operational integration between divisions: the Oil Cake Processing Division supplies de-oiled coconut cake, a critical raw material for the Animal Feed Division, supporting supply-chain security

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Raw material price volatility — High and unpredictable prices for essential feed ingredients (soybean meal, rice bran, maize, copra cake) driven by supply-chain disruptions, irregular weather, government interventions, geopolitical factors and competing demand from food/biofuel industries continue to pressure margins; near-term visibility on corrections remains limited.
- Subsidised-competitor landscape in Kerala — Government and Cooperative feed players in Kerala create an uneven competitive landscape; government control over milk prices limits dairy farmers' capacity to absorb feed cost increases, impacting demand for the Company's products in this segment and constraining pricing flexibility.
- Exchange-rate fluctuations on imported copra cake — A significant portion of copra cake is imported from Sri Lanka and the Philippines; volatility in INR/USD and INR/PHP exchange rates poses material risk to procurement costs, with a weaker rupee eroding margins, especially during periods of domestic price pressure.
- Copra cake availability / coconut oil price volatility — While rising coconut oil prices support the Oil Cake Processing Division's profitability, scarcity of de-oiled copra cake - driven by rising Asia-Pacific demand and, going into FY27, a lower coconut crop yield - poses a challenge to feed production and raises the risk of supply constraints and pricing pressure.
- Labour dependency and escalating costs — Labour-intensive operations in Kerala face ongoing shortages, resulting in rising wage costs and operational strain, especially in margin-sensitive segments; mitigated through mechanisation, productivity initiatives and long-term wage settlements.
- Working capital and credit exposure — Growth in the Ice Cream and Dairy Divisions has increased dealer and distributor credit exposure; delays in receivables or distributor defaults may create liquidity pressures despite controlled credit policies and periodic reviews.
- Weather and agricultural shifts — Monsoon failures, erratic rainfall, and shifts in cropping patterns towards higher-value cash crops reduce the availability of essential oilseeds and grains, tightening raw-material supply for the feed business.
- Structural decline of the core Kerala market — Shrinking cattle population and declining commercial dairy farming in Kerala - the Company's key home market - alongside government-controlled milk procurement prices, structurally constrain feed and milk demand, requiring the Company to lean on Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and new geographies for growth.
